description:
# Reusable communication-channel integration testing, scaffolding and agent workflow
Status: implementation plan approved in this conversation; this ticket materializes the plan. Creating the epic does not implement it or authorize committing/pushing/merging.

## Objective and observable outcome
One reusable ExUnit harness must run the same real message/agent/reply and persisted-history scenarios against WhatsApp, Mattermost and Telegram. The only simulated services are communication providers and the existing LLM HTTP boundary. A future production adapter (Teams is the example, not an implementation deliverable here) joins by implementing a test-driver behaviour and passing the common suite. A Mix generator scaffolds the test integration and a repository skill guides completion and ALL-provider regression validation.

## Explicit decisions from the user (2026-10-21)
- Initially requested planning without BW or code changes; the latest request explicitly authorizes creating this detailed epic and its implementation tasks.
- Use a general test-support driver behaviour plus conformance tests for concrete fake-provider drivers.
- No changes to production/application behaviour. The final agreed tooling exceptions are exactly lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/**. All harness/fake/fixture/template/test changes belong under test/.
- Skill must be in this checkout's .agents/skills, NOT test/skills and NOT a user-level installation. Mix task belongs in lib/mix/tasks, NOT test/support/mix/tasks.
- The generator creates a fake-provider/test-driver skeleton for an already available production adapter. It must not create a production Teams adapter, install a dependency, or change the provider registry in config.
- Run the shared suite for EVERY registered test driver, including existing providers, when adding or changing an integration or its automation.

## Superseded proposal: DO NOT implement a transport-option production refactor
The earlier proposal to extend Bridge/JidoChatBridge/WhatsApp connection-option forwarding was withdrawn after discovering existing test seams.
- test/support/whatsapp.ex already contains WhatsAppFlowAdapter, which delegates to Jido.Chat.WhatsApp.Adapter and injects WhatsAppFlowTransport for authentication/listener/send/edit/typing. Reuse it. Saved-connector fetch_connection_details_for_config/1 remains untouched.
- Mattermost uses native WebSocket callback frames and a local HTTP server; reuse test/support/mattermost_history_fixture.ex.
- Telegram already points the real adapter's HTTP requests to a local server in test/zaq/channels/telegram_history_delivery_test.exs; use native webhook updates for the new ingress scenarios.
No URL-based WhatsApp protocol emulator is required.

## Production path under test
native provider input -> real adapter parsing/listener or webhook handler -> JidoChatBridge/State -> CommunicationBridge -> NodeRouter -> Engine identity/routing/capture/admission -> Agent.Api/Executor/Factory/Jido with existing local LLM mock -> Engine finalization -> NodeRouter :deliver_outgoing -> Channels.Api -> selected saved connector -> Bridge.fetch_connection_details_for_config -> JidoChatBridge -> real adapter (test transport wrapper for WhatsApp) -> fake recipient -> DeliveryConfirmation -> canonical history.
Do not enter at Executor.run, construct canonical Incoming/Outgoing in lieu of provider ingress, insert the answer/transcript directly, or stub internal routing to make the new shared scenarios pass. Such calls can arrange unrelated fixtures only where already allowed by the testing handbook.

## Evidence and reuse map (verify live source before work)
- test/support/whatsapp.ex and test/zaq/channels/linked_device/integration_flows_test.exs: real adapter delegation, simulated recipient mailbox, direct/group LLM round trips; runtime_contracts_test.exs and whatsapp_onboarding_test.exs are existing consumers to preserve.
- test/support/mattermost_history_fixture.ex; test/zaq/channels/mattermost_shared_history_integration_test.exs; person_credential_ingress_integration_test.exs: native ingress, HTTP, identity, permissions, runtime cleanup.
- test/zaq/channels/telegram_history_delivery_test.exs and jido_chat_bridge/telegram_reaction_webhook_test.exs: real HTTP delivery and webhook envelope shape (do not copy the latter's NodeRouter fake).
- test/support/openai_stub.ex, multi_agent_openai_stub.ex and tool_calling_llm_stub.ex: reuse LLM server/response builders. Basic reply tests need text responses; tool-calling is an additional representative scenario, not mandatory for every message.
- test/support/integration_agent.ex creates conversation_enabled: false: do not use it unchanged for channel routing or change its established default. New channel fixtures must explicitly create conversation_enabled: true and active: true.
- test/support/data_case.ex owns SQL Sandbox/event-registry setup. test/support/delivery_diagnostics.ex provides bounded failure diagnostics; keep raw credentials/private runtime data out of new diagnostics.
- Jido.Chat.AdapterTestKit is adapter-package conformance support, not a substitute for the real ZAQ integration suite; reuse relevant assertions where compatible.
- test/test_helper.exs excludes :integration by default. Do not tag the new suite :integration or add any default exclusion.
- mix.exs already compiles test/support in :test. No mix.exs edits are needed.
- Related BW zaq-kts owns the general communication-integration guide; link/reuse it as context only, do not take over its docs work. QUALITY_SCORE channel notes are stale relative to source; do not treat them as current implementation facts.

## Exact ownership and expected files
New:
test/support/channels/integration/driver.ex
test/support/channels/integration/session.ex
test/support/channels/integration/registry.ex
test/support/channels/integration/case.ex
test/support/channels/integration/fixtures.ex
test/support/channels/integration/assertions.ex
test/support/channels/integration/contract.ex
test/support/channels/integration/README.md
test/support/channels/integration/drivers/{mattermost,telegram,whatsapp}.ex
test/support/channels/integration/templates/{driver.ex.eex,provider_test.exs.eex}
test/zaq/channels/integration/{driver_contract,round_trip,transcript,delivery_failure}_test.exs
test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/{mattermost,telegram,whatsapp}_test.exs
test/mix/tasks/zaq_test_gen_channel_test.exs
lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex
.agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/SKILL.md
Optional only when needed for isolation/scripting without changing current defaults:
test/support/whatsapp.ex; test/support/mattermost_history_fixture.ex.
No production lib/zaq/** or lib/zaq_web/** edits, no deps/**, config/**, migrations, mix.exs, mix.lock, CI, or docs/** changes in this epic. Additional focused tests may be added under the listed test directories. Runtime temp directories are per-test and cleaned up.

## Frozen driver contract
Namespace Zaq.TestSupport.Channels.Integration; concrete modules Drivers.Mattermost, Drivers.Telegram, Drivers.WhatsApp.
- start(opts): accepts owner_pid and unique scope; returns {:ok, handle}. Handle contains provider atom, actual configured adapter module (real or delegating test wrapper), ingress_mode, connector_attrs, sender facts, direct/shared room coordinates, and opaque provider state. Starts only the fake external endpoint/process; owns no ZAQ business persistence.
- connect(handle, context): {:ok, connected_handle} | {:error, reason}. Context includes the saved connector and fixture identities. This explicit second phase is necessary because local endpoints start before connector creation, while WhatsApp pairing/runtime startup needs the saved connector. Drive real bridge startup/authentication as appropriate and return only after readiness. No UI browser is needed; reuse public pairing/runtime APIs and fake scan mechanics. All started processes/resources must be registered for Case cleanup.
- emit(session, message_spec): {:ok, emission} | {:error, reason}. Message spec carries content, room (:direct/:shared), sender, unique source id, explicit timestamp, mention flag, and optional thread/reply reference. Build native provider payloads and use real ingress. Emission returns native source/room coordinates and correlation metadata; it cannot manufacture an answer or canonical history.
- script(session, script): :ok | {:error, reason}. Queue provider responses by operation and contract-relevant request match; allow send/edit success, controlled failure and explicit optional unsupported capabilities. Never accidentally consume a terminal-reply failure with a preceding typing/status request.
- deliveries(session): ordered list of recorded attempts. Each entry includes sequence, operation, provider, connector/source scope, native room/thread/reply target, provider message id where available, text, outcome and sanitized native payload. Include failed attempts; distinguish create/edit/typing. Shared assertions derive final visible state from successful create/edit operations, not from call count alone.
- capabilities(): map. :direct and :shared are mandatory for initial three drivers; :threads, :thread_root_lookup and :edits explicitly describe optional provider semantics. Required scenarios cannot be disabled. Evidence must agree with the actual adapter API.
Session stores driver/handle, scope, connector, Person, configured agent, observer and resource ownership. Scope/id correlation is test-owned, not inferred from fixed global constants.

## Suite registration and deterministic execution
Registry.all/0 is the sole test-driver list, deterministic by provider name, initially Mattermost/Telegram/WhatsApp. Each entry maps provider atom -> driver module. All four shared test modules enumerate it and identify provider/scenario in ExUnit names and tags. No separate per-file provider lists.
Registry conformance detects duplicates, missing behaviour/callbacks, driver files absent from registry and invalid capability declarations. Use expected directory/module conventions, not an unbounded app/source scan.
Report production-configured communication providers with no driver as explicit coverage gaps. Existing other providers are not automatically implemented or silently claimed covered. New scaffold registration is immediate and incomplete callbacks FAIL clearly; never use skip/pending or silently remove an entry to get green.
All real-runtime suites start async: false because of application env, shared Sandbox mode, singleton ServerManager and existing WhatsApp fake. Restore each mutated env key to its exact prior present/absent value, stop owned agent/bridge/listener resources before sandbox teardown, and scope provider data by connector/profile. Never stop unrelated runtimes.
Wait on actual events/receipts/worker completion and bounded assert_receive/Task.await/barriers, not sleeps or polling. Subscribe before emission. A provider receipt alone may precede Engine confirmation: await routing/finalization/confirmation completion before asserting canonical transcript placement. Negative/no-reply assertions need a processed-ingress barrier before refute_received.

## Required scenario matrix
Every provider: direct prompt -> model input -> correct recipient reply -> direct transcript; mentioned room prompt -> shared transcript/reply; passive room capture under mention_required with no Agent call; follow-up context with exact permitted prior text; duplicate provider input with one execution/one canonical input and one final answer; connector/chat/person isolation; unauthorized history access; send failure and edit failure where supported, without false confirmed history placement.
Transcript assertions use Conversations.list_canonical_messages/3 for permitted reads and independent expected values for strategy, author, role, order, source ids, connector/native scope and parent/thread links. Direct history uses participant grants; shared history uses the real channel-history permission contract. Setup must not hide automatic-membership bugs with manual grants; explicit manual-grant scenarios are separately named.
Generated/private execution records are not the same as confirmed externally visible assistant transcript placements. Failure tests must assert this distinction.
Mattermost adds bot-root vs human-root mention policy. Telegram adds chat-local message-id collisions and HTTP update semantics. WhatsApp adds PN/LID/group JID facts, self/history suppression and real delegating wrapper calls. Optional threads are exercised only using evidenced provider contracts.
At least one real registered tool-call scenario reuses ToolCallingLLMStub; assertions prove the tool result, not only the requested call.
Property coverage stays focused: source-id/scope isolation and generator name/path validation over broad input sets. Do not multiply full LLM/process startup for hundreds of generated cases.

## Generator contract
Command: mix zaq.test.gen.channel teams --adapter Jido.Chat.Teams.Adapter [--dry-run].
Developer task can compile needed modules without app.start; it must not start Repo, listeners, agents or provider connections. It must not depend on loading/compiling test/support modules in the dev environment.
Validate a lowercase provider identifier and a fully qualified module name, confirm the adapter module is available and implements core adapter identity/ingress/send APIs, and validate every output plus the registry edit before writing. An unavailable production adapter is an actionable error with zero changes; installing Teams is outside this epic.
Outputs: drivers/teams.ex; integration/providers/teams_test.exs; one sorted registry entry. Templates contain explicit implementation failures and native ingress/delivery TODOs. Never invent Teams payloads or label a fake implementation complete.
Only accept the provider, --adapter and --dry-run; no --force, no arbitrary output path, no user-controlled template eval. Refuse existing output/registration, invalid names, traversal/symlink escapes and missing/ambiguous registry edit markers. --dry-run produces planned paths/diff with zero changes.
Use deterministic dedicated registry markers and literal entries so the task can update it as text/AST without executing test code. Preflight all paths; stage writes and roll back only files/edits created by this invocation if a later write fails. Do not overwrite concurrent edits.
Task tests use isolated temporary projects/fixtures and an installed or synthetic test adapter; do not require a real Teams dependency or provider account.

## Skill contract
Exact path: .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/SKILL.md.
Describe only adding/completing a communication test integration using this generator. Follow the skill-creator workflow for the skill; do not create a ZAQ runtime agent skill or expose a new Jido Action/tool.
Workflow: inspect current adapter + existing fixtures; confirm adapter available; run dry-run then generator; fill native ingress and fake boundary code; implement provider-specific assertions; run driver conformance and targeted cases; then ALL registered provider cases plus affected existing regressions; check allowed paths and record results.
Stop and report if completion requires app/dependency changes, changed existing assertions, or missing production support. Do not bypass failures by stubbing NodeRouter/Agent/history, skipping tests or unregistering drivers. Existing unrelated installed providers missing drivers are explicitly reported as coverage gaps.
Keep the skill concise, with links to the test README/contracts and policy owners; templates and workflow commands have one authoritative implementation.

## Action reuse assessment
Harness orchestration: REUSE existing adapter/bridge/Engine/Agent/history APIs through the production path; new helpers are LOCAL-ONLY ExUnit fixtures, fake external providers and assertions. Inputs are synthetic provider messages/identities, outputs are observed provider attempts plus real persisted state. Errors stay visible. State lives in sandbox/per-test fake processes; no agent-tool/workflow consumer or new application Action.
Generator: LOCAL-ONLY developer filesystem operation owned by Mix.Tasks.Zaq.Test.Gen.Channel. Existing lib/mix/tasks tasks demonstrate task conventions but perform unrelated operations; no domain/Jido Action matches generating test source. Filesystem effects are bounded to test paths and no network/app-start is needed.
Skill/documentation: NOT APPLICABLE to executable domain Actions; it invokes the developer task and tests without exposing tools.

## Validation and completion
Follow docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md for per-step quality/isolated validation, review, post-review coverage-upper handoff and final mix precommit; do not waive those gates. No new browser E2E/UI approval issue is required because no product UX changes are planned.
Full suite command: mix test test/zaq/channels/integration; generator tests: mix test test/mix/tasks/zaq_test_gen_channel_test.exs. Existing provider/support regressions listed in child issues must also pass. No :integration default exclusion.
Final diff must satisfy the explicit path allowlist, and production/dependency/config files must be unchanged. Preserve existing assertions and helper defaults. Record known test/environment blockers honestly; do not declare completion on partial passes.
Build sequencing is recorded in child dependencies. The epic stays open until every required child, review, coverage and final validation is complete. It does not block its own children.

## Planning provenance
This plan replaces the conversation-only proposal; source paths were inspected and BW searches found no existing epic for this harness. Current branch: feat/channel-mock-tests. No application/test/tooling implementation has been performed while creating this plan.

## Implementation issue index and dependency graph
1. zaq-o9d.1 — Define driver/session contracts and deterministic test-driver registry
2. zaq-o9d.2 — Build real-runtime channel IntegrationCase, fixtures and completion barriers
3. zaq-o9d.3 — Implement Mattermost provider driver using native frames and local HTTP
4. zaq-o9d.4 — Implement Telegram provider driver using native webhooks and local Bot API
5. zaq-o9d.5 — Implement WhatsApp driver by reusing the existing delegating adapter and fake transport
6. zaq-o9d.6 — Run the common message and agent round-trip matrix for every registered driver
7. zaq-o9d.7 — Verify direct/shared transcript contents, permissions and source-scope isolation
8. zaq-o9d.8 — Exercise provider delivery failures and test isolation across all registered adapters
9. zaq-o9d.9 — Add the channel test-driver Mix scaffold generator with safe test-only output
10. zaq-o9d.10 — Create the repository skill for scaffolding and completing channel integration tests
11. zaq-o9d.11 — Review the complete harness, generator and skill against the agreed scope
12. zaq-o9d.12 — Complete post-review coverage handoff, final validation and human approval


This is an intentionally serial delivery sequence: the drivers share Case/Registry and establish stable examples before common regression scenarios, templates and skill instructions are finalized. It avoids simultaneous edits to those shared files and makes each completed step reviewable. Only zaq-o9d.1 has no implementation prerequisite; later children are blocked by their immediate prerequisite. The parent epic is organizational and must never be a blocker of its children. No cyclic/diamond dependencies are intended. Review approval precedes coverage; final human approval follows final validation. The full epic remains open until all twelve children are complete.

## Planning validation
Verified all 12 child issues are open, parented to zaq-o9d, and have self-ID title prefixes, implementation/test/mock/documentation/reuse/completion sections. Verified 11 directed prerequisite edges, reciprocal blocked_by/blocks fields and an acyclic graph. The sole unblocked implementation child is zaq-o9d.1. This installed bw ready currently lists the new parent epic rather than its first child; inspect bw show zaq-o9d --only children and bw show zaq-o9d.1 --only summary,blockedby to select the first implementation task. Do not change parent status or dependency direction just to alter the ready display.
Repository worktree was clean after planning; no application, test, Mix-task or skill files were written and no application tests were run for this Beadwork-only task.

comments.text: Implementation checkpoint: zaq-o9d.1-.3 completed with required quality/focused validations. Shared test contracts, session/fixtures/completion observer, registry, strict fake response ledger and complete Mattermost driver are implemented. Telegram driver is implemented but zaq-o9d.4 is blocked by zaq-kxd and zaq-imv, with failing native end-to-end reproducers preserved. mix q passes; final relevant regression snapshot is 75 tests + 2 properties, with exactly those 2 new Telegram failures; existing regressions pass. All 18 added working-tree files are under test/, no production/dependency/config edits or commits. WhatsApp, full common matrix, generator and skill are not yet implemented. The explicit no-production-change scope prevents fixing the blockers inside this epic; do not silently mask them or advance blocked tasks as complete. See zaq-o9d.4's detailed checkpoint and blocker tickets before resuming.

User clarified that two Telegram regressions must not halt independent implementation. Dependency correction: WhatsApp now depends on completed Mattermost infrastructure, while Telegram acceptance blocks final review. Continue .5 through .10; preserve both reproducer failures and production-only fix boundary. Graph: .3 -> .5 -> .6 -> .7 -> .8 -> .9 -> .10 -> .11; .4 -> .11 -> .12. No production changes authorized.

Independent implementation now includes WhatsApp, registry-wide round-trip/transcript/failure scenarios, the compile-only generator and repository skill. Thread coverage found zaq-gr2 (real Telegram/ExGram thread-id type mismatch). .7 remains acceptance-blocked, and blocks .11 rather than .8 so delivery/generator/skill work continues. No scenarios skipped and no production fixes made.

Final independent-work checkpoint: implemented framework, all three native provider drivers, automatic shared matrix, direct/shared transcript and permission coverage, native source-scope property, send/edit failure and lifecycle isolation, dev Mix generator/templates, and repository skill. Final combined run: mix test test/zaq/channels/integration test/mix/tasks/zaq_test_gen_channel_test.exs plus existing Mattermost shared-history, Jido delivery, Telegram history/Markdown, WhatsApp linked-device/runtime/Markdown and onboarding regressions => 181 tests, 4 properties, exactly 3 failures. All failures are preserved new Telegram reproductions: zaq-kxd, zaq-imv, zaq-gr2. Existing tests pass unchanged. mix q passes; git diff --check passes; skill validator passes; documentation links valid. Allowed-path audit: 31 changed/new files, no application/config/dependency changes and no existing test assertion changes. Only tracked modification is backward-compatible test/support/whatsapp.ex; tooling exceptions are the named Mix task and .agents skill. .4 and .7 remain open for affected Telegram acceptance; .11 review and .12 coverage/final validation remain pending. No commit/push performed. Final precommit is intentionally not claimed because review/coverage prerequisites and real defect fixes are unresolved. Test-only scope forbids fixing the application/dependency defects; all independent authorized implementation has continued to completion.
